status: lighting-02 reviewed; shadow-recovery-limit preferred unchanged, pending final atmosphere/geology source recheck; no profile/source changes by this leaf

matchedReview.verified: All 16 native 1280x720 PNGs viewed. Manifest reports hardware AMD Radeon 780M, one production source and no errors. Each of four views has all four exact full lighting profiles; PNG CRCs, dimensions and SHA-256 values match the manifest.
matchedReview.selectionStatus: Preferred lighting profile for integration recheck, not final visual acceptance of the scene or full route.
matchedReview.rationale: The brighter fill bracket is the only candidate that improves the backlit near forest. Its cooler fill lifts the darkest canopy while the slightly softer sun preserves warm cliff/sand detail. Balanced and clear-dimensional darken the same backlit regions; their reduced haze increases apparent saturation but does not meet the shadow-readability priority.

perView.control: Warm ochre rock and olive trees retain grain, but foliage interiors are dark.
perView.balanced: A small cooler/less ochre change; no decisive interior-detail gain.
perView.dimensional: Slightly stronger dark edges, with little added structural reading.
perView.shadowRecovery: Cleaner green foliage and more readable trunk/interior transitions. Warm rock grain survives; it does not visibly become chalky.

perView.control: Pale cliff and dark forest separate mostly through albedo; distant ridge remains muted.
perView.balanced: Lower haze is visible but the lower-right forest is more closed.
perView.dimensional: More dark/light separation, but dark masses lose readability and geometric limitations remain.
perView.shadowRecovery: Best lower-right forest readability and natural green/ochre separation. Existing cliff form remains legible, but lighting does not repair the rejected geology.

perView.control: Canopy is dark yellow-olive above a warm cliff and detailed cool water.
perView.balanced: Less orange rock; foliage still closes down slightly.
perView.dimensional: Harder shadow contrast with more near-black canopy pixels.
perView.shadowRecovery: Best shadow detail and cleaner green foliage, with slightly cooler water and retained sand/cliff grain. The image remains warm in direct light.

perView.control: Warm sunset and cool sea work, but near trees read as a dense dark band.
perView.balanced: Near and far backlit forests darken; haze reduction is not shadow recovery.
perView.dimensional: Darkest backlit near forest, with little useful extra internal structure.
perView.shadowRecovery: Near-tree interiors brighten while the far ridge stays close to the control. Sun/reflection warmth remains, and the near forest does not become a uniform grey patch.

measurements.method: Pillow read-only sampling of the supplied PNGs; sRGB bytes decoded to linear, then Rec.709 luminance. Fixed rectangles contain mixed scene materials, not semantic masks. Values are display-referred after ACES and cannot establish physical radiance or overall quality.
measurements.thresholds: Near-black means all RGB bytes <=5. Clipped means any RGB byte >=254; none of the five sampled rectangles contained such pixels for any candidate. This is not a whole-frame clipping claim.

remainingLimits: The same-source batch includes shore pass 2 and coastal understory enabled, per the driver; preference applies to that common scene state.

Cloud/geology 02 shapes remain rejected independently. Their next source changes can alter PMREM, direct occlusion and visible depth, so rerender preferred lighting against the same-source canonical control afterward.
Recheck the four matched views plus opening 0 and follow-up 3/6/9/12 before promoting a global canonical profile. Do not introduce camera-specific exposure changes.
The large grey cloud ceiling at 19.5 and pale rounded geology remain visible. No lighting profile in this batch establishes the requested final scene quality.

baselineCaveat: Both supplied manifests verify this source and hardware rendering, but do not record effective lighting. The declared control baseline is the checked-in canonical profile.

observations.finding: Backlit forest is muted olive/brown; near foliage detail remains visible, while the distant sea/horizon takes a broad warm-grey veil.
Water already has useful turquoise depth. Forest shadows are densely packed; boosting overall exposure would also lift pale shore and glitter.
Beach rock shadows remain legible. Water color is stronger than the vegetation; preserve the subdued foam and warm sand detail.
Warm cliff and olive woodland sit above a cool but grey reflective sea. Background ridge separation is weak.
Near sand grain and water detail survive. Direct-lit cliff is pale peach, while tree masses are dark olive with little cool shadow separation.
The same warm pale cliff/dark olive canopy split persists; stronger global saturation would amplify sand and foliage yellow together.
Sun/reflection alignment and blue foreground sea are coherent. Backlit ridges are muted, clouds dominate with broad grey-white areas.
Local foliage/trunk detail is available. Broad cliff faces remain rounded and pale; lighting alone cannot supply missing geological planes or cavities.
Pale cliffs separate from forest mainly by albedo. Distant terrain is grey-green; added grade must not substitute for structural relief or actual cast shadows.

sourceResponse.finding: All proposed keys are public lighting controls; colors are converted by THREE.Color and changes invalidate the sky probe/cloud shadows.
sunColor/sunIntensity also affect cloud radiance. skyColor/groundColor/skyIntensity affect only HemisphereLight, not visible sky or its probe.
Visible clear sky and in-scattering share fixed directional bayClearSky colors. fogDensity changes height-dependent extinction, not haze hue.
environmentIntensity scales MeshStandard PMREM lighting generated from the visible sky; raising it broadly can wash shaded materials.
Ocean samples reflectedSky directly, so environmentIntensity is not an ocean saturation/brightness control. Sun controls affect glitter/foam and fogDensity affects eye-to-water air.
The baseline linear path resolves radiance before one ACES/sRGB conversion. Exposure acts globally; no existing saturation, contrast, shadow-lift or tone-curve profile controls exist.
Plan settings accumulate. Supply each complete alternative lighting object on every row; preserve the same full base profile for all non-lighting controls.

alternatives.rationale: First choice: less orange direct light, more cool hemisphere fill, slightly less broad PMREM fill and haze. Lower sun/exposure protects the pale rock and sand while cooler fill should reveal foliage and recesses.
alternatives.rejectIf: Canopy becomes cyan/flat, foliage hue loses its natural olive component, or the reduced air removes near/far ridge separation. The sunset must retain warm light and a readable reflection path.

alternatives.rationale: Stronger shape bracket: keep exposed direct-light luminance close to baseline, reduce broad ambient and air, and modestly strengthen cool hemisphere fill. This should test whether new geological planes read without an exposure increase.
alternatives.rejectIf: Tree masses merge into black, cracks read only as dark paint, rock highlights lose grain, or cliff improvement is merely an increase in bright/dark albedo contrast.

alternatives.rationale: Upper fill bracket, primarily for diagnosing canopy readability: stronger cooler fill and a softer, less orange sun, with most baseline aerial depth retained. Prefer the first alternative unless this supplies necessary shadow information.
alternatives.rejectIf: Foliage looks chalky, trunk/leaf contrast collapses, cliffs flatten, warm/cool separation looks artificially blue/orange, or broad grey fill increases.

inputRatioCaveat: Calculated from THREE.Color linear RGB and Rec.709 luminance, then multiplied by the stated intensity/exposure. These are input-term ratios, not predicted pixel changes. Environment ratio excludes the changed probe radiance; reflected sunlight and nonlinear ACES responses need actual renders.

matchedBatch.order: For each view: same-source canonical baseline, then alternatives in priority order. Match resolution, time, camera, geometry, materials, clouds, shadow settings and linear output path.

perViewGuidance.criterion: Read distinct illuminated planes and cool recesses while retaining rock grain. Judge the same geometry first with the canonical light.
Retain sand/foam detail and turquoise water; tree interiors must become more readable without pale haze.
Keep warm backlight, cool foreground water and ordered ridge depth. Avoid camera-specific exposure fixes; final flight uses one coherent lighting profile.
Preserve rock shadow shape, natural green canopy, and existing water hue; do not compensate for shoreline geometry with lighting.

matchedBatch.acceptance: Inspect matched native PNGs and fixed material ROIs; reject new channel clipping, lost shadow texture or lost highlight grain. A brighter whole-frame histogram alone is not improvement. Profile proposals remain unaccepted until this batch is reviewed.

heldFixed: Cloud coverage/morphology, shadow-map/bias/casters, all surface and geology controls, camera, sun direction, linear output, sample scale, coastal reflection and Island source-response remain on the parent's same-source baseline. No global saturation/contrast grade or material recoloring is proposed.
knownLimit: If the warm-grey horizon persists, these controls cannot directly repair its fixed spectral colors. That needs the atmosphere owner's shared sky/aerial/probe response review, followed by another matched batch; do not disguise the issue by darkening exposure.
